concerns.concern: Joule heating is ruled out only because the suppression does not depend on bath temperature. There is no estimate of the local temperature rise from 1 to 4 µW dissipated at the gate apex, no thermal-model prediction of the r0 shift between bath temperatures, and no direct comparison with a resistive heater.
concerns.quote: Joule heating caused by the leakage current can be excluded because the quenching does not depend on temperature.

concerns.concern: Field-emitted electrons through vacuum are ruled out only by gate-polarity symmetry. That is insufficient: with the island as cathode, electrons land on the gate apex 80 nm away. The leakage curves should be fitted to Fowler-Nordheim emission, and r0 checked against drifts in onset voltage.
concerns.quote: with the island as cathode the electrons land on the gate apex 80 nm away, which polarity symmetry alone does not separate.

concerns.concern: The argument against a direct electric-field effect relies on Fig. 3b, which mixes different powers. Within each temperature set r0 rises steeply with |VG|. r0 should be plotted against VG at fixed power, using the constant-power runs.
concerns.quote: r0 against VG at fixed P: part (Fig. 3b mixes powers)

concerns.concern: The Fig. 4e control, with leakage current but supposedly no field at the superconductor, uses only one gate pair and does not quantify the electric field at the island. The simulated |E| at the island edge should be given.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4e, one gate pair, field at the island not quantified

concerns.concern: The confirming r0(P) data from the second and third devices (D2a, D2b) appear only in the Supplementary figures, not in the paper itself. One of these datasets should be shown in the main text beside Fig. 3a.
concerns.quote: Show one D2a or D2b r0(P) set beside Fig. 3a

concerns.concern: The paper does not count how many devices were fabricated per run, how many were imaged, or how many showed the effect. It also does not count cooldowns, say whether the nanowire D1 was imaged, or explain how the Fig. 2c and Fig. 4 scans were chosen.
concerns.quote: Devices fabricated and imaged per run, and cooldowns ("several cool-downs", p. 3), are not counted.

concerns.concern: The paper does not say whether any devices or cooldowns were set aside, for example for leakage breakdown, vortex pinning or probe problems, or why.
concerns.quote: If any devices or cooldowns were set aside (for example for leakage breakdown, vortex pinning or probe problems), why?

concerns.concern: Only one bias field was used, and no reason is given for the power and gate ranges shown. It is unclear whether other fields, other bath temperatures, powers above about 4.5 µW, or gates G2 to G5 were measured.
concerns.quote: One bias field; no reason given for the power and gate ranges shown.

concerns.concern: The authors should report whether transport GCS was measured on nanowire D1 and at what gate power its critical current vanished. This would allow the µW imaging powers to be compared with transport on the same film.
concerns.quote: Did you measure the transport GCS on the nanowire D1, and at what gate power did its critical current vanish

concerns.concern: The r0 extraction procedure is described only in the Supplementary Materials, not in the paper itself. Data are available only on request, and no code is linked.
concerns.quote: the r0 extraction is in the Supplementary Materials [25], not in the v1 PDF
